THE SPLIT PLATE / RECIPE

High-Protein One-Pan Breakfast Skillet

510 cal. 45g protein. 10 minutes. One pan. Eggs + Gilbert's Caprese + Lao Gan Ma.

YIELD1 serving
TOTAL TIME10 min
COOK METHODSee method
EST. / SERVING~510 cal | ~45g protein

Ingredients

Ingredients

  • Cooking spray (Chosen Foods avocado oil)
  • 2 Gilbert's Craft Sausages Caprese Chicken Sausage links (basil + mozzarella + sun-dried tomato variant)
  • 3 large eggs

Ingredients — continued

  • Kosher salt, to taste
  • 1 tsp Lao Gan Ma Fried Chili in Oil (NOT a tablespoon — 1 tsp is the macro lever)
  • Optional: black pepper or extra chili flakes

You want a hot breakfast that feels like real food (not a shake or bar), 45g of protein, and you have 10 minutes with one pan. 2 sausage links + 3 eggs + a spoonful of Lao Gan Ma — that's the entire system. Skip the chili crisp for kids; everything else stays the same.

Method

  1. 1.SPRAY THE PAN. Nonstick skillet over medium heat. Hit with cooking spray.
  2. 2.ADD SAUSAGE. 2 Gilbert's Caprese chicken sausage links into the pan. Cook 3-4 min, turning to brown all sides + warm through. The chicken sausage is pre-cooked — you're crisping the exterior, not cooking through raw meat.
  3. 3.CRACK IN THE EGGS. 3 large eggs cracked directly into the skillet around the sausage links. Keep medium heat — too hot and the whites burn before the yolks set.
  4. 4.SEASON. Pinch of kosher salt over the eggs. Black pepper if using.
  5. 5.ADD CHILI CRISP. 1 tsp Lao Gan Ma Fried Chili in Oil spooned over the eggs (focus on the crispy bits, light on the oil — the oil adds ~80 cal per tablespoon and you only want ~25 cal worth).
  6. 6.COVER + SET. Lid on. 2-4 min until whites are fully set and yolks are still jammy (or longer if you want them firm). Don't peek every 30 sec — open once at the 2-min mark.
  7. 7.SERVE HOT. Slide everything onto a plate or eat straight from the skillet. The macro headline is 510 cal / 45g protein assuming 2 Gilbert's links + 3 eggs + 1 tsp Lao Gan Ma — any deviation shifts the math.

SPLIT PLATE SERVING

Adult: Serve the adult portion as described above.

Kid: Serve the kid portion as described above.

If something fails

Eggs are rubbery / overcooked: Heat was too high or you covered too long. Medium heat, 2-3 min covered max for jammy yolks. Lid traps steam — it cooks fast.

Whites won't set without burning the bottom: Heat too high. Drop to medium-low + cover. Steam sets the whites from above without crisping the bottom.

Chili crisp made the dish way over 510 cal: You used a tablespoon instead of a teaspoon. 1 tbsp Lao Gan Ma = ~80 cal / 9g fat. 1 tsp = ~25 cal / 3g fat. The tsp portion is the macro-architecture lever — measure it.

Sausage links are dry / over-crisped: You cooked them too long before adding the eggs. Gilbert's chicken links are pre-cooked — 3-4 min to brown is plenty. Add the eggs at the 3-min mark even if the sausage looks pale.

Macros came in higher than 510 cal: Most likely cause: (1) 4th egg or 3rd sausage link, (2) over-portioned chili crisp (tbsp instead of tsp), or (3) over-spray of cooking oil. The 2/3/1 ratio is the budget — don't drift.

Kid wouldn't eat it because of the red flecks: Skip the Lao Gan Ma entirely on the kid plate. Same skillet, same sausage, same eggs — just no chili crisp on their side. Plate theirs first, then add the chili to your portion.

Storage and reheating

Store: Best made fresh — 10 min is fast enough. Don't batch. Cooked eggs hold ~24 hours but the texture degrades.

Reheat: N/A — eggs reheat poorly. If you must: 30 sec microwave covered, but expect rubbery whites and over-set yolks.

Lasts: N/A — cook per serving.

Headline total: 500 cal / 45P / 34F / 4 net C — rounded to 510 / 45 in the headline. Fat/carbs/fiber values flagged 'estimated' because (1) sausage link weights vary slightly across packs, (2) Lao Gan Ma scoop varies by oil-vs-crispy-bits ratio. Core ratio — locked

2 Gilbert's Caprese chicken sausage links + 3 large eggs + 1 tsp Lao Gan Ma. This is the system. Add more chili crisp and you blow the fat budget; add a 4th egg and you blow the cal budget. Lock the 2/3/1 ratio.

Flavor target

Brown the sausage links + crack 3 eggs around them + 1 tsp Lao Gan Ma scattered over the eggs + cover until whites set + jammy yolks. Don't flip the eggs — lid does the work. Don't drown in chili oil — 1 tsp is the right portion for the macro target.

Adult plate | Kid plate

Adult plate

Adult

Full recipe as written — 2 Gilbert's links + 3 eggs + 1 tsp Lao Gan Ma. Adults get the chili-crisp finish.

Kid plate

Kid

Same 2 sausage links + 2-3 eggs, but SKIP the Lao Gan Ma entirely (the chili oil is the spicy adult layer). Kids get plain salt + a small piece of toast or fruit on the side. ~400 cal / 30-35g protein depending on egg count.

Brands I use

Gilbert's Craft Sausages
Caprese Chicken Sausage (basil + part-skim mozzarella + sun-dried tomato, 10 oz pack / 4 links — ~13-15g protein per link)
Pre-cooked chicken sausage so you crisp instead of cooking through raw meat. Mediterranean flavor profile (basil + mozzarella + sun-dried tomato) pairs surprisingly well with the Sichuan chili crisp finish — the umami carries it. Other Gilbert's SKUs work but the macro math assumes Caprese.
Lao Gan Ma
Fried Chili in Oil (~25 cal / 3g fat per 1 tsp; AVOID the 1 tbsp portion = ~80 cal / 9g fat)
The flavor shortcut for the dish. Sichuan-style fried chili in soybean oil with crispy bits. 1 tsp gives the heat + texture + umami without blowing the fat budget. Cross-recipe — pairs with eggs, rice, dumplings, noodles, anywhere you want chili heat.
Chosen Foods
Avocado Oil Spray
Neutral cooking spray, ~0-5 cal per spray. Nonstick coating for the skillet so the eggs slide cleanly. Cross-recipe staple.
